_comment: Owner-approved record changes from the held-review process (approved 27 Oct 2026). Applied by tools/apply_approved_changes.py and allowed — exactly and only — by the disclosure safeguards in engine/tests via engine/approved_changes.py. History is only ever appended to. Not covered here, so still blocked: somatic physiotherapy (on hold), the SPI-1005 score (separate consistency review), any other rating, rank or record.

fields.from: Company reports ≥30% patient-reported tinnitus severity improvement — from an open-label extension, so high bias risk and not a loudness measurement.
fields.to: In two placebo-controlled trials in people with Ménière's disease, self-rated tinnitus loudness (the 0–10 loudness question of the TFI) improved no more with SPI-1005 than with placebo (Phase 3, 220 people: −0.8 vs −0.9 points; Phase 2b: about a third improved by 2 or more points in each group, placebo included). Registry results, not yet peer-reviewed. There are no loudness data in other kinds of tinnitus.

appendHistory.change: loudness.level: limited → none (shown as 'None shown'); loudness.summary rewritten (Ménière's population named); registry results NCT04677972 and NCT03325790 added as study records
appendHistory.reason: Held review 2026-10-27 (classification-review-spi-1005-loudness-2026-10-27), approved by the owner 27 Oct 2026: the 'limited' rating rested on an open-label severity outcome, which is not a loudness measure; two placebo-controlled trials in Ménière's disease that measured self-rated loudness (TFI item 2) show no difference from placebo. Evidence score, tier and distress rating unchanged by this review (distress is under a separate held review).

fields.from: Observational reports of reduced audibility/awareness; controlled percept-level evidence is weak.
fields.to: Self-rated loudness and loudness matches have been reported to fall after fitting in before–after studies, more so when the fitting is objectively verified (2022 meta-analysis). No placebo-controlled trial has tested this, and in UNITI's hearing-aid arm measured loudness did not change while distress scores fell.

appendHistory.change: loudness.summary rewritten to describe the direct loudness evidence (wording only)
appendHistory.reason: Held review 2026-10-27 (classification-review-hearing-aids-loudness-2026-10-27), approved by the owner 27 Oct 2026: the previous wording ('audibility/awareness') had no cited source. No score, tier, level, ranking, or numerical result changed.

fields.from: Same open-label PRO data; no blinded tinnitus outcome has been published.
fields.to: In two placebo-controlled trials in people with Ménière's disease, tinnitus impact (TFI) improved about as much with placebo as with SPI-1005 (Phase 3, 220 people: −7.9 vs −6.6 points; Phase 2b: more people improved on placebo than on either dose). An open-label extension reported improvement, but without a comparison group. Registry results, not yet peer-reviewed. There are no data in other kinds of tinnitus.

fields.from: The most advanced drug with a tinnitus-relevant claim — but its trials are in Meniere's disease, and the tinnitus data are unblinded.
fields.to: The most advanced drug with a tinnitus-relevant claim — but its trials are in Meniere's disease, and in placebo-controlled trials tinnitus improved no more than with placebo.

fields.from: A Phase 3 program with BTD earns 2/5 for tinnitus specifically: the tinnitus outcomes are open-label, company-reported, and in a Meniere's population. The ongoing Phase 3 (NCT06859788) is open-label single-group — it cannot produce controlled tinnitus evidence.
fields.to: A Phase 3 program with BTD earns 2/5 for tinnitus specifically: in its placebo-controlled Phase 2b and Phase 3 trials (registry results, Ménière's disease) the tinnitus outcomes were secondary and showed no advantage over placebo; the positive tinnitus result comes from an open-label extension. The ongoing Phase 3 (NCT06859788) is open-label single-group — it cannot produce controlled tinnitus evidence.

appendHistory.change: distress.level: limited → none (shown as 'None shown'); distress.summary, oneLiner and scoreRationale corrected (they described the tinnitus data as open-label/unblinded only)
appendHistory.reason: Held review 2026-10-27 (classification-review-spi-1005-distress-2026-10-27), approved by the owner 27 Oct 2026: two placebo-controlled trials in Ménière's disease (NCT04677972, NCT03325790) show no distress (TFI) advantage over placebo; the only positive result is an uncontrolled open-label extension. The 3 Sept 2026 note that SPI-1005 had 'zero controlled tinnitus data' is superseded by these registry results (the Top 10 outcome is unaffected). Evidence score (2/5) and tier unchanged; a separate consistency review of the score is open.

fields.from: Self-rated loudness and loudness matches have been reported to fall after fitting in before–after studies, more so when the fitting is objectively verified (2022 meta-analysis). No placebo-controlled trial has tested this, and in UNITI's hearing-aid arm measured loudness did not change while distress scores fell.
fields.to: In UNITI, a large randomised trial (461 people), people given hearing aids alone rated their tinnitus 1.4 points quieter on a 0–10 scale after 12 weeks (95% CI 0.6 to 2.1); the trial did not report a statistical comparison with the other treatments. Loudness measured by matching it to a tone did not change, and a small trial with a counselling-only comparison also found little change in matched loudness. Before–after studies report reductions, more so with verified fittings. There is no placebo-controlled test.

appendHistory.change: loudness.summary corrected: separates UNITI's self-rated loudness reduction from unchanged tone-matched loudness; no claim of superiority over other treatments (wording only)
appendHistory.reason: Held review 2026-10-27 (classification-review-hearing-aids-loudness-level-2026-10-27), approved by the owner 27 Oct 2026: the earlier wording said UNITI's hearing-aid arm showed no loudness change, which is true only of tone-matched loudness (Schiele 2025); self-rated loudness fell 1.4 points (Schoisswohl 2025, Nat Commun). UNITI reports no statistical loudness comparison between treatments (supplement Table S17). Loudness level 'Limited', score, tier and rank unchanged.

fields.to: Tinnitus data: in the placebo-controlled Ménière's trials (registry results, secondary outcomes) tinnitus improved no more than with placebo; the reported improvement comes from an uncontrolled open-label extension

studiesAdded.title: STOPMD-3: SPI-1005 (ebselen) Phase 3 in Ménière's disease — ClinicalTrials.gov posted results
studiesAdded.journal: ClinicalTrials.gov posted results (first posted 26 June 2026; no peer-reviewed publication found)
studiesAdded.design: Randomized, quadruple-masked, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial (84 days)
studiesAdded.primaryOutcome: Low-frequency hearing (pure-tone audiometry) and Words-in-Noise (co-primary); tinnitus outcomes secondary

results.summary: Tinnitus loudness (TFI item 2, 0–10): mean change −0.8 with SPI-1005 vs −0.9 with placebo. TFI total: −7.9 vs −6.6. No statistical analysis posted for the tinnitus outcomes.
results.detail: Self-rated loudness and tinnitus impact changed by similar amounts in both groups. Ménière's disease population.

studiesAdded.limitations: Registry-only reporting; Ménière's disease, not primary tinnitus; tinnitus outcomes secondary; loudness is a single TFI item.

studiesAdded.title: SPI-1005 (ebselen) Phase 2b in Ménière's disease — ClinicalTrials.gov posted results
studiesAdded.journal: ClinicalTrials.gov posted results (first posted 14 August 2023; no peer-reviewed publication found)
studiesAdded.n: 149 enrolled; 124 analysed (41 placebo / 42 SPI-1005 200 mg / 41 SPI-1005 400 mg twice daily)
studiesAdded.design: Randomized, quadruple-masked, placebo-controlled Phase 2b trial (8 weeks)
studiesAdded.primaryOutcome: Hearing, Words-in-Noise, TFI, tinnitus loudness (TFI item 2) and vertigo (each listed as primary on the registry)

results.summary: Tinnitus loudness improved by ≥2 points (TFI item 2) in 14/41 (34%) on placebo, 15/42 (36%) on 200 mg and 14/41 (34%) on 400 mg. TFI improved by ≥10 points in 20/41 (49%), 19/42 (45%) and 13/41 (32%).
results.detail: No advantage over placebo on loudness or tinnitus impact. Ménière's disease population.

studiesAdded.limitations: Registry-only reporting; Ménière's disease, not primary tinnitus; loudness is a single TFI item; responder analysis only.
